newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybeans end mixed on uncertainties.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybeans end mixed on uncertainties.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mixed on Tuesday on uncertain short term market trend, traders said.
The most actively traded July 1997 contract ended at an intraday low of 3,299 yuan ($398) per tonne, losing 46 yuan. It opened at a high of 3,300 yuan per tonne.
The July contract is due to deliver on July 22.
September rose 33 to 3,291 yuan per tonne, November fell 32 to 3,248, the January 1998 contract rose 40 to 3,260 and March was unchanged at 3,200 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume rose to 14,700 tonnes from 13,700 tonnes.
Soybeans opened mixed and moved at opening levels for most of the session, traders said.
"Many investors liquidated their positions in the July contract today with the approach of the delivery date," one trader said.
"Retail investors for quick profits dominated trading in other contracts due to a lack of market-moving news," he added.
Traders said they expected soybeans to continue moving in a narrow range in the next few days.
